package com.tlc.notification.service; import java.util.Collection; /** *

* Provides the push notification services. * The implementation may vary (Azure Web PubSub, FCM, Azure Notification Hub, etc.) * but consumers interact only through this generic interface. *

* * @version 1.0 */ public interface PushNotificationService { /** *

* Sends a push notification message to a specific connection. *

* * @param connectionId the target connection identifier * @param message the message payload to send */ void sendToConnection(String connectionId, String message); /** *

* Sends a push notification message to all connections of a specific user. *

* * @param userId the target user identifier * @param message the message payload to send */ void sendToUser(String userId, String message); /** *

* Broadcasts a push notification message to all connected clients in a group. *

* * @param group the target group name * @param message the message payload to send */ void sendToGroup(String group, String message); /** *

* Broadcasts a push notification message to all connected clients. *

* * @param message the message payload to send */ void broadcastToAll(String message); /** *

* Adds a connection to a group. *

* * @param group the group name * @param connectionId the connection identifier to add */ void addConnectionToGroup(String group, String connectionId); /** *

* Removes a connection from a group. *

* * @param group the group name * @param connectionId the connection identifier to remove */ void removeConnectionFromGroup(String group, String connectionId); /** *

* Adds a user to a group. *

* * @param group the group name * @param userId the user identifier to add */ void addUserToGroup(String group, String userId); /** *

* Removes a user from a group. *

* * @param group the group name * @param userId the user identifier to remove */ void removeUserFromGroup(String group, String userId); /** *

* Generates a client access token (URL) for a user to connect to the push notification service. *

* * @param userId the user identifier * @param roles the roles/permissions to grant (e.g., group join/send permissions) * @return the client access URL containing the access token */ String generateClientAccessUrl(String userId, Collection roles); /** *

* Checks if a specific connection is currently active. *

* * @param connectionId the connection identifier * @return true if the connection exists, false otherwise */ boolean connectionExists(String connectionId); /** *

* Closes a specific connection. *

* * @param connectionId the connection identifier to close * @param reason the reason for closing the connection */ void closeConnection(String connectionId, String reason); /** *

* Stops the push notification service and releases all acquired resources. *

*/ void stop(); }

package com.tlc.notification.service; import com.tlc.notification.service.push.ClientAccessRequest; import com.tlc.notification.service.push.ConnectionRequest; import com.tlc.notification.service.push.PushGroupRequest; import com.tlc.notification.service.push.PushRequest; /** *

* Provides push notification services through a generic, pluggable interface. * All method parameters are request objects with extensible options maps, * so providers (Azure Web PubSub, FCM, etc.) can consume additional params * without ever requiring an interface change. *

* * @version 1.0 */ public interface PushNotificationService { /** *

* Sends a push notification message based on the target defined in the request. * Supports sending to a specific connection, user, group, or broadcasting to all * depending on {@link PushRequest#getTargetType()}. *

* *

Example usage:

* 
     * pushNotificationService.send(PushRequest.builder()
     *     .toUser("user123")
     *     .payload("{\"event\":\"update\",\"data\":{...}}")
     *     .option("contentType", "application/json")
     *     .option("ttl", 30)
     *     .build());
     *
* * @param request the push request containing target, payload, and extensible options */ void send(PushRequest request); /** *

* Manages group membership (add/remove connections or users to/from groups). * The action and any provider-specific options are encapsulated in the request object. *

* *

Example usage:

* 
     * pushNotificationService.manageGroup(PushGroupRequest.builder()
     *     .action(PushGroupRequest.Action.ADD_USER)
     *     .group("org-123")
     *     .targetId("user456")
     *     .option("ttl", 3600)
     *     .build());
     *
* * @param request the group management request */ void manageGroup(PushGroupRequest request); /** *

* Generates a client access token/URL for a user to connect to the push service. * Provider-specific options (token lifetime, custom claims, etc.) go in the request's options map. *

* *

Example usage:

* 
     * String url = pushNotificationService.generateClientAccess(ClientAccessRequest.builder()
     *     .userId("user123")
     *     .roles(List.of("webpubsub.joinLeaveGroup", "webpubsub.sendToGroup"))
     *     .option("tokenLifetimeInMinutes", 60)
     *     .build());
     *
* * @param request the client access request * @return the client access URL or token string */ String generateClientAccess(ClientAccessRequest request); /** *

* Manages a connection (check existence, close, etc.). * Provider-specific options (close reason code, grace period, etc.) go in the request's options map. *

* *

Example usage:

* 
     * boolean exists = pushNotificationService.manageConnection(ConnectionRequest.builder()
     *     .action(ConnectionRequest.Action.CHECK_EXISTS)
     *     .connectionId("conn-abc")
     *     .build());
     *
* * @param request the connection management request * @return true for CHECK_EXISTS if connection is active; false otherwise. For CLOSE, always returns true on success. */ boolean manageConnection(ConnectionRequest request); /** *

* Stops the push notification service and releases all acquired resources. *

*/ void stop(); }

* Defines the scope at which rate limiting is applied. * This determines how the rate limit key is resolved. *

* * @author Thalaimalai Pandiyan T * @version 1.0 */ public enum RateLimitScope { /** * Rate limit is applied globally across all requests for a given endpoint. * All users and orgs share the same counter. */ GLOBAL, /** * Rate limit is applied per client IP address. * Each unique IP has its own counter. */ PER_IP, /** * Rate limit is applied per organization. * All users within an org share the same counter. */ PER_ORG, /** * Rate limit is applied per user within an organization. * Each user in each org has its own counter. */ PER_USER_IN_ORG }

---
## Execution Examples
### Using APPROACH 1 (Direct CSV Export)
```bash # Execute the migration query psql -U postgres -h localhost -d crm_database < product_to_clickhouse_migration.sql
# Output CSV file with formatted headers ls -lh /tmp/dim_product_clickhouse.csv
# Verify CSV header head -1 /tmp/dim_product_clickhouse.csv ```
**Expected Output**: ``` "ID","ORG_ID","NAME","PRODUCT_CODE",...,"COMPANY_FIELDS" ```
### ClickHouse Import
```sql -- Insert CSV data into ClickHouse INSERT INTO DIM_PRODUCT FROM INFILE '/tmp/dim_product_clickhouse.csv' FORMAT CSV;
-- Verify import SELECT COUNT(*) FROM DIM_PRODUCT; ```
---
## Timestamp Conversions
All timestamp fields are automatically converted from PostgreSQL milliseconds to ClickHouse DateTime format:
```sql -- PostgreSQL stores timestamps as milliseconds since epoch -- Conversion formula: to_char(to_timestamp(mp.created_time / 1000.0), 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS')
-- Result format: '2024-03-30 15:45:30' ```
---
## JSON Field Structure
Custom fields are aggregated into JSON format with field IDs:
```json { "1": {"fieldId": 101, "value": "field_value"}, "2": {"fieldId": 102, "value": "another_value"} } ```
---
## Data Volume Handling
For migration of 200K+ records:
### Recommended Approach Use `product_to_clickhouse_optimized.sql` with batch processing:
```bash # Step 1: Create staging table psql -U postgres -h localhost -d crm_database < product_to_clickhouse_optimized.sql
# Step 2: Export staging table psql -U postgres -h localhost -d crm_database << EOF \copy (SELECT * FROM dim_product_staging) TO '/tmp/products.csv' CSV HEADER; EOF
# Step 3: Import to ClickHouse cat /tmp/products.csv | clickhouse-client --query="INSERT INTO DIM_PRODUCT FORMAT CSV" ```
---
## File Locations Summary
| File | Location | Purpose | |------|----------|---------| | complete_migration_queries.sql | `/home/thalaimalai_pandiyan/Desktop/february/ /(copy/)/` | Full migration query with all CTEs | | product_to_clickhouse_migration.sql | `/home/thalaimalai_pandiyan/Desktop/february/ /(copy/)/` | Direct CSV export approach | | product_to_clickhouse_optimized.sql | `/home/thalaimalai_pandiyan/Desktop/february/ /(copy/)/` | Batch processing approach | | product_migration_guide.md | `/home/thalaimalai_pandiyan/Desktop/february (copy)/` | Detailed documentation | | clickhouse_contact_tables_structure.csv | `/home/thalaimalai_pandiyan/Desktop/february (copy)/` | Contact table structure reference |
---

1. ✅ Execute migration query on PostgreSQL 2. ✅ Verify CSV output with formatted headers 3. ✅ Import CSV to ClickHouse 4. ✅ Run validation queries 5. ✅ Set up incremental CDC sync for updates

* *

 *         .action(PushGroupRequest.Action.ADD_USER)

 *         .action(ConnectionRequest.Action.CHECK_EXISTS)
 *         .connectionId("conn-abc")
 *         .build());
 * }

* * @version 1.0 */ public interface PushManagementService extends PushNotificationService { /** *

* Manages group membership (add/remove connections or users to/from groups). * The action and any service-specific options are encapsulated in the request object. *

* * @param request the group management request */ void manageGroup(PushGroupRequest request); /** *

* Manages a connection (check existence, close, etc.). * Service-specific options (close reason code, grace period, etc.) go in the request's options map. *

* * @param request the connection management request * @return true for CHECK_EXISTS if connection is active; false otherwise. For CLOSE, always returns true on success. */ boolean manageConnection(ConnectionRequest request); }

package com.tlc.notification.service; import com.tlc.notification.service.push.PushRequest; /** *

* Base interface for push notification services. * Contains only the common methods that EVERY push notification implementation must support, * regardless of the underlying technology (Azure Web PubSub, FCM, native WebSocket, etc.). *

* *

* Specialized capabilities are defined in segregated interfaces: *

    *
  • {@link com.tlc.notification.service.PushManagementService} — group/connection management
    • *
  • {@link com.tlc.notification.service.PushAccessService} — client access token/URL generation
    • *
* Implementations may selectively implement these based on their capabilities. *

* * @version 1.0 */ public interface PushNotificationService { /** *

* Sends a push notification message based on the target defined in the request. * The payload type is generic ({@code T}) — callers can send String, JSON objects, * DTOs, byte[], etc. The implementation handles serialization. *

* *

Example usage:

* 
     * // Send a String payload
     * pushService.send(PushRequest.<String>builder()
     *     .toUser("user123")
     *     .payload("{\"event\":\"update\"}")
     *     .option("contentType", "application/json")
     *     .build());
     *
     * // Send a typed DTO payload
     * pushService.send(PushRequest.<NotificationEvent>builder()
     *     .toGroup("org-456")
     *     .payload(new NotificationEvent("refresh", data))
     *     .build());
     *
* * @param request the push request containing target, payload, and extensible options * @param the type of the message payload */ void send(PushRequest request); /** *

* Stops the push notification service and releases all acquired resources. *

*/ void stop(); }

The type parameter {@code T} represents the request/payload type for sending messages. * Each implementation binds to its own request type (e.g., {@code PushRequest}).

* *

* Extended capabilities are defined in {@link PushManagementService} which adds * group management, connection management, and client access token generation. *

* * @param the type of the send request * @version 1.0 */ public interface PushNotificationService { /** *

* Sends a push notification message. * The request type is generic — implementations define what they accept * (e.g., {@code PushRequest}, {@code PushRequest}, or any custom request). *

* * @param request the request containing target, payload, and extensible options */ void send(T request); /** *
